title: Texture-Based Nesting | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our Nesting Features in 2025.0 allows you to easily nest your patterns based on your textures placements within the 3D window.  

Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Chapters: 
00:00 - Introduction
01:10 Where to find Nesting features
01:43 Regular Nesting 
02:26 Texture Based Nesting
07:24 Print Based Nesting 
08:35 Lock in Place Nesting

summary: ```markdown # Texture-Based Nesting | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe and I have some great updates to share with you regarding our nesting capabilities and prints that have all been updated in our 2025.0 version. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Garment Setup Alright, so here I have my garment and I've worked really hard to get this print and everything laid out exactly how I like it. My texture is exactly where I want it to be. The lines are hitting where I want them, and all of that is really nice. I love it! ## Designer Concerns Now, if you're a designer, tech designer, or even a production person, what you might be feeling is a little bit of anxiety. You might be thinking, "Okay, now if I have to go to print layout and nest this, all of this might get ruined." But what we have now done is, if you've set it up in your 3D window like this and you like it, you can actually ensure that the nesting follows the setup in your 3D window. ## Pattern Selection and Property Editor All you have to do is select the patterns that you want to have follow your 3D window setup. Then, over in your property editor on the right-hand side, right below fabric and fabric grain direction, you'll see “pattern matching.” Here, you can decide if you want it to be texture-based, print-based, or lock in place. ### None Option Let’s first discuss what happens if you select "none." If you choose none and go into your print layout to nest, you’ll see that the texture gets changed. This is because it's trying to find the best consumption amount for you, and it’s nesting for that rather than matching your textures together from your 3D window. ## Texture-Based Pattern Matching Don’t worry, we have another file! Again, we’re going back to this one, which has everything that I want and is perfect. So with this, we’ll select those pattern pieces. In your property editor, underneath fabric pattern matching, I’m going to select “textured base.” You would select this if your pattern or fabric has the texture you want to follow. ### Locking Mechanism If you have the base color map for your texture and it's not an all-over print, you will want to pick "texture" here in your pattern matching. Selecting "textured base" will automatically lock the pattern matching. You might be wondering what that means. It means that if I go to my edit texture tool and try to move this around, I can't because this is locked. The texture will stay locked for you, which is really nice. You can still scale it if you want, but you won’t be able to move it. ## Print Layout Nesting If you go into your print layout, those pattern pieces are also locked. You can't move them in your print layout, ensuring they follow exactly what's going on in your 3D window. If I want to nest and say "nest current fabric," Clo reads the entire fabric, finds the matching parts, and nests the patterns in the best consumption for you, matching exactly what you did in your 3D window. You can do this again to see if there’s any better consumption or anything like that. This is pretty good! It also works if you add multiple pattern pieces. For instance, if I have a total of five, I can nest current fabric for all of the patterns. You will see them all following the same texture placement. ## Example Demonstration This is a huge win! This is really going to help because you can see how extensive it will be. You can determine how long it will take, which is crucial for pricing and all of that information. Let’s demonstrate with an example using texture nesting. Suppose you have your shirt, front body, placket, and another shirt laid out perfectly. You can select all these pieces and also the back. Again, go to your property editor and enable “textured face.” ### Adjusting in Print Layout Let’s say you forgot to do this in your 3D window or simulation mode, and you go into print layout. You can select all these pattern pieces, right-click, and choose “pattern matching” followed by “textured face.” This will automatically lock them for you. You can perform this action both in your simulation mode and in your print layout mode. It’s just a right-click, then you can unlock all patterns or choose the appropriate matching options. ## Print Options Now, let’s talk about the print option. If I open up my object browser and see plain fabric alongside an added print, you can select all pattern pieces in your 3D window and choose “print base” under fabric pattern matching if the texture you’re following is an added print. ### Locking for Specific Patterns Locking is particularly useful for jeans or graphic placements. In this workflow, let’s go straight into print layout because there are washes within this print. I will select my pattern piece and place it exactly where I want it. Once I'm satisfied with the placement, I can select both pieces, right-click, and choose “pattern matching” followed by “lock in place.” For the rest of the patterns, I’m fine with however they get nested, so I’ll just hit “nest current fabric,” and all the other pattern pieces will get nested for me. ## Conclusion This update is especially great as it simplifies production and pricing processes. It ensures you don’t have to worry about anything getting changed when nesting in your print layout. Thank you all so much for watching! If you have any questions, please feel free to use the comment section down below. Check out the rest of our videos on our Clo YouTube channel. Thanks again, and don’t forget to like and subscribe. Keep having fun in Clo! ```
